```{r code, results = "hide"}
# the compiled core and the R files of next_steps/ (every file is shown in full in Section 4)
if (!exists("params")) {                                   # running the chunks one by one
  header <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("som_next_steps.Rmd")$params
  params <- lapply(header, function(x) if (is.list(x)) x$value else x)
}
p <- params
cores <- if (p$cores > 0) p$cores else max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 2)
needed <- c("Rcpp", "digest", "jsonlite", "htmltools", "xfun", "plotly", "DT", "Rmpfr")
missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, TRUE, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) stop("please install: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
Sys.setenv(PKG_LIBS = "-lquadmath -lmpfr -lgmp")           # the 128-bit and the MPFR arithmetic of the precision ladder
Rcpp::sourceCpp("next_steps/ns_core.cpp", cacheDir = "next_steps/.cpp_cache")
Rcpp::sourceCpp("next_steps/ns_mpfr.cpp", cacheDir = "next_steps/.cpp_cache")
for (f in c("ns_data.R", "ns_maps.R", "ns_quality.R", "ns_bench.R", "ns_precision.R", "ns_report.R")) source(file.path("next_steps/R", f))
```

```{r run-all, include = FALSE}
# Everything is computed here, before the first line of text, and cached in next_steps/cache under a key
# made from the code and the settings. The first knit takes about two hours of CPU time (half of it
# soft-DTW); next_steps/run_benchmark.R computes the same cache outside the knit, on all cores.
QUICK <- isTRUE(p$quick)
SIZES <- if (QUICK) c(5, 7) else c(5, 7, 10, 14)
REF <- if (10 %in% SIZES) 10 else max(SIZES)                   # the size the text quotes
CACHE_DIR <- if (QUICK) "next_steps/cache_quick" else "next_steps/cache"
seeds <- seq_len(p$seeds)
datasets <- load_datasets()
time_all <- system.time(res <- compute_all(datasets, VARIANTS, SIZES, seeds, p$rlen, cores, dir = CACHE_DIR))[["elapsed"]]
bench <- res$bench; fits <- res$fits; det <- res$detection
n_maps <- nrow(unique(bench[, c("dataset", "variant", "size", "seed")]))
cpu_min <- sum(unique(bench[, c("dataset", "variant", "size", "seed", "seconds")])$seconds) / 60

# the precision ladder: the tutorial's small CBF (with the Rmpfr check of the MPFR core) and the PD stand-in
LADDER <- if (QUICK) list(cbf = list(size = 5, rlen = 4), pd = list(size = 5, rlen = 1), pd_raw = list(size = 5, rlen = 1)) else list(cbf = list(size = 7, rlen = 20), pd = list(size = 7, rlen = 4), pd_raw = list(size = 7, rlen = 4))
ladder <- compute_ladder(datasets, p$mpfr_bits, LADDER, dir = CACHE_DIR)
small_cbf <- ladder$small_cbf

# the verified idea catalogue of the brainstorm (next_steps/ideas/ideas.json), if it is there
ideas <- if (file.exists("next_steps/ideas/ideas.json")) jsonlite::fromJSON("next_steps/ideas/ideas.json", simplifyVector = FALSE) else NULL

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- helpers for the text
JUDGE_LAB <- c(euclid = "Euclidean", dtw = "DTW", own = "own distance")
VIEWS <- list(                                             # measure, judge, how the advantage over the control is taken
  list(id = "ari_own",  m = "ARI",    j = "own",    higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "ARI, each map with its own distance"),
  list(id = "ari_dtw",  m = "ARI",    j = "dtw",    higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "ARI, all read with DTW"),
  list(id = "ari_eu",   m = "ARI",    j = "euclid", higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "ARI, all read with the Euclidean distance"),
  list(id = "nmi_own",  m = "NMI",    j = "own",    higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "NMI, own distance"),
  list(id = "pur_own",  m = "purity", j = "own",    higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "Purity, own distance"),
  list(id = "qe_eu",    m = "QE",     j = "euclid", higher = FALSE, kind = "rel",  label = "QE, all judged with the Euclidean distance"),
  list(id = "qe_dtw",   m = "QE",     j = "dtw",    higher = FALSE, kind = "rel",  label = "QE, all judged with DTW"),
  list(id = "ev_eu",    m = "EV",     j = "euclid", higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "EV (explained variance), Euclidean"),
  list(id = "te_own",   m = "TE",     j = "own",    higher = FALSE, kind = "pp",   label = "TE, own distance"),
  list(id = "te_dtw",   m = "TE",     j = "dtw",    higher = FALSE, kind = "pp",   label = "TE, all read with DTW"),
  list(id = "kl_eu",    m = "KL",     j = "euclid", higher = FALSE, kind = "rel",  label = "KL (Kaski-Lagus), Euclidean"),
  list(id = "kl_dtw",   m = "KL",     j = "dtw",    higher = FALSE, kind = "rel",  label = "KL (Kaski-Lagus), DTW"),
  list(id = "tp_own",   m = "TP",     j = "own",    higher = FALSE, kind = "diff", label = "|TP| (topographic product), own distance"),
  list(id = "used_own", m = "used",   j = "own",    higher = TRUE,  kind = "pp",   label = "Share of units used, own distance"),
  list(id = "trust",    m = "trust",  j = "euclid", higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "Trustworthiness (Euclidean neighbourhoods)"),
  list(id = "cont",     m = "cont",   j = "euclid", higher = TRUE,  kind = "diff", label = "Continuity (Euclidean neighbourhoods)"),
  list(id = "secs",     m = "seconds", j = "own",   higher = FALSE, kind = "rel",  label = "Seconds to train"))
names(VIEWS) <- sapply(VIEWS, `[[`, "id")
val <- function(ds, v, size, m, j) {                       # one measure of one map, every seed in order
  b <- bench[bench$dataset == ds & bench$variant == v & bench$size == size & bench$judge == j, ]
  b <- b[order(b$seed), ]; x <- b[[m]]; if (m == "TP") abs(x) else x
}
mean_of <- function(ds, v, size, view) mean(val(ds, v, size, VIEWS[[view]]$m, VIEWS[[view]]$j), na.rm = TRUE)
adv_of <- function(ds, v, size, view) {                    # the variant against its family's control, seed by seed
  vw <- VIEWS[[view]]; ctrl <- VARIANTS[[v]]$family
  a <- val(ds, v, size, vw$m, vw$j); b <- val(ds, ctrl, size, vw$m, vw$j)
  n <- min(length(a), length(b)); a <- a[seq_len(n)]; b <- b[seq_len(n)]
  adv <- switch(vw$kind, diff = if (vw$higher) a - b else b - a, pp = 100 * (if (vw$higher) a - b else b - a),
                rel = 100 * (if (vw$higher) (a - b) / b else (b - a) / b))
  data.frame(seed = seq_len(n), v = a, c = b, adv = adv)
}
wins_of <- function(ds, v, size, view) { a <- adv_of(ds, v, size, view)$adv; c(better = sum(a > 0, na.rm = TRUE), worse = sum(a < 0, na.rm = TRUE), n = sum(!is.na(a))) }
# the same against any other map (for the DTW-SOM against the online SOM, say)
wins_vs <- function(ds, v, ctrl, size, view) {
  vw <- VIEWS[[view]]; a <- val(ds, v, size, vw$m, vw$j); b <- val(ds, ctrl, size, vw$m, vw$j)
  n <- min(length(a), length(b)); a <- a[seq_len(n)]; b <- b[seq_len(n)]
  d <- if (vw$higher) a - b else b - a
  c(better = sum(d > 0, na.rm = TRUE), worse = sum(d < 0, na.rm = TRUE), n = sum(!is.na(d)))
}
# words for a count of seeds: 'better on 4 of 5 seeds, worse on 1'
tally <- function(w) if (w[["n"]] == 0) "not run" else sprintf("better on %d of %d seeds, worse on %d", w[["better"]], w[["n"]], w[["worse"]])
tally_short <- function(w) if (w[["n"]] == 0) "not run" else sprintf("%d of %d", w[["better"]], w[["n"]])
judge_word <- function(w) { n <- w[["n"]]; if (n == 0) "not run" else if (w[["better"]] >= 0.8 * n && w[["better"]] > w[["worse"]]) "clearly better" else if (w[["worse"]] >= 0.8 * n && w[["worse"]] > w[["better"]]) "clearly worse" else "level" }
# one phrase per data set: 'CBF clearly worse (0 of 5), partial discharges level (3 of 5), gestures ...'
by_ds <- function(v, view, size = REF, ctrl = NULL) paste(sapply(names(datasets), function(k) {
  w <- if (is.null(ctrl)) wins_of(k, v, size, view) else wins_vs(k, v, ctrl, size, view)
  sprintf("%s %s (%s)", SHORT[[k]], judge_word(w), tally_short(w)) }), collapse = ", ")
# on how many data sets a variant was clearly better / clearly worse than its control on a view
count_ds <- function(v, view, size = REF) { j <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) judge_word(wins_of(k, v, size, view))); c(better = sum(j == "clearly better"), worse = sum(j == "clearly worse"), n = length(j)) }
best_variant <- function(ds, size, view, among = names(VARIANTS)) {
  m <- sapply(among, mean_of, ds = ds, size = size, view = view)
  m <- m[is.finite(m)]
  if (!VIEWS[[view]]$higher) m <- -m
  list(id = names(m)[which.max(m)], label = VARIANTS[[names(m)[which.max(m)]]]$label, value = abs(m[which.max(m)]))
}
SHORT <- c(cbf = "CBF", pd = "Partial discharges", gestures = "Gestures", gunpoint = "GunPoint")
SHORT <- SHORT[names(datasets)]
det_mean <- function(v) mean(det$AUROC[det$variant == v])
v_lab <- function(v) VARIANTS[[v]]$label
nn_floor <- sapply(datasets, function(d) sapply(c("euclid", "dtw"), function(judge) {
  Dm <- cross_dist(d$X, d$X, d, judge_args(d, judge)); diag(Dm) <- Inf
  mean(d$cls[max.col(-Dm, ties.method = "first")] == d$cls) }))
```

```{r headline-numbers, include = FALSE}
# the numbers of the box below, all from the results of this knit (REF x REF maps unless said otherwise)
pd_best_ari <- best_variant("pd", REF, "ari_own")
pd_eu_ari   <- mean_of("pd", "euclid", REF, "ari_own"); pd_dtw_ari <- mean_of("pd", "dtw", REF, "ari_own")
ge_best_ari <- best_variant("gestures", REF, "ari_own"); ge_eu_ari <- mean_of("gestures", "euclid", REF, "ari_own")
det_best <- names(which.max(sapply(names(VARIANTS), det_mean)))
det_corona_eu <- mean(det$AUROC_corona[det$variant == "euclid"])
# the two temperatures against their controls, judged with DTW for soft-DTW (the control's own distance)
soft_fit <- by_ds("softdtw", "qe_dtw"); soft_cls <- by_ds("softdtw", "ari_dtw"); soft_te <- by_ds("softdtw", "te_dtw")
ann_te <- by_ds("anneal", "te_own"); ann_qe <- by_ds("anneal", "qe_eu"); ann_cls <- by_ds("anneal", "ari_own")
temps_won <- sum(sapply(c("softdtw", "anneal", "dtw_anneal"), function(v) sum(sapply(c("qe_dtw", "qe_eu", "te_own", "ari_own", "kl_dtw", "kl_eu"), function(vw) count_ds(v, vw)["better"]))))
# the distances against the ONLINE SOM on the classes (the DTW-SOM is its own family's control)
THR <- ceiling(0.8 * p$seeds)                              # 'clearly': at least this many seeds, and more better than worse
dist_vs_eu <- function(k) { v <- setdiff(names(VARIANTS)[sapply(VARIANTS, `[[`, "group") == "distance"], "euclid")
  w <- sapply(v, function(x) wins_vs(k, x, "euclid", REF, "ari_own")); v[w["better", ] >= THR & w["better", ] > w["worse", ]] }
temps_n <- 3 * 6 * length(datasets)
clear_pd <- dist_vs_eu("pd"); clear_ge <- dist_vs_eu("gestures"); clear_cbf <- dist_vs_eu("cbf")
size_flip  <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) sapply(SIZES, function(s) best_variant(k, s, "ari_own")$id))
LD <- c(cbf = "small CBF", pd = "PD stand-in (asinh)", pd_raw = "PD stand-in, raw pressure")
lad_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(LD), function(k) cbind(data = k, ladder[[k]]$table)))
fp32_first <- lad_tab[lad_tab$precision == "fp32" & lad_tab$mode == "euclid", c("data", "first_flip", "flips", "drift")]
fp64_flips <- lad_tab[lad_tab$precision == "fp64", c("data", "mode", "flips", "drift")]
gap_small  <- sapply(ladder[names(LD)], function(l) c(fp32 = mean(l$gap < 2^-23, na.rm = TRUE), fp64 = mean(l$gap < 2^-52, na.rm = TRUE), min = min(l$gap, na.rm = TRUE)))
raw32 <- lad_tab[lad_tab$data == "pd_raw" & lad_tab$mode == "euclid" & lad_tab$precision == "fp32", ]
raw64 <- lad_tab[lad_tab$data == "pd_raw" & lad_tab$mode == "euclid" & lad_tab$precision == "fp64", ]
raw32d <- lad_tab[lad_tab$data == "pd_raw" & lad_tab$mode == "dtw" & lad_tab$precision == "fp32", ]
flip_words <- function(flips, S) if (flips == 0) sprintf("the same winner at every one of the %s steps", format(S, big.mark = ",")) else sprintf("another winner at %d of the %s steps", flips, format(S, big.mark = ","))
first_words <- function(r, S) if (is.na(r$first_flip)) sprintf("never chose a different winner in %s steps either, and ended within %s of the reference", format(S, big.mark = ","), formatC(r$drift, digits = 1, format = "e")) else sprintf("first chose a different winner at step %d and then went its own way (prototypes %s apart at the end)", r$first_flip, formatC(r$drift, digits = 1, format = "e"))
e1 <- function(x) formatC(x, digits = 1, format = "e")
mp_name    <- sprintf("MPFR %d-bit", p$mpfr_bits)
mpfr_secs  <- lad_tab$seconds[lad_tab$precision == mp_name & lad_tab$data == "cbf" & lad_tab$mode == "euclid"]
fp64_secs  <- lad_tab$seconds[lad_tab$precision == "fp64" & lad_tab$data == "cbf" & lad_tab$mode == "euclid"]
rmpfr_row  <- lad_tab[grepl("Rmpfr", lad_tab$precision), ]
```

The project built a SOM from scratch, made it a DTW-SOM, and tested fourteen
variants on twelve data sets, plus chaos, rings and tearing maps. The growing
DTW-SOM was the best of its family and DTW the biggest single lever; chaos
and tearing lost to the plain controls that do the same job. This page asks
**what to build next** for two uses: **detecting and classifying partial
discharges** from their waveforms, and **classifying movements** from sensor
series. It has three parts:

1. **The ideas** (Sections 1 to 3): what the benchmarks already decided, a
   catalogue of improvements gathered from seven angles (distances, physics,
   the structure of the map, partial-discharge engineering, movement
   recognition, numerical precision, and evaluation), each with the plain
   control it must beat seed by seed, and a bridge from physics to the code.
2. **A demonstrator** (Sections 4 to 7): the online SOM rewritten once, with
   nine distances in the winner choice *and* in the update, six training
   ingredients that each test one idea, four map sizes, all the project's
   measures plus trustworthiness, continuity and detection AUROC, on
   `r length(datasets)` data sets (`r paste(sapply(datasets, "[[", "title"), collapse = "; ")`),
   `r p$seeds` seeds each, every variant judged against
   its family's control with the same start and order of items.
3. **The precision ladder** (Section 8): the same map in fp32, fp64, 80-bit,
   128-bit and `r p$mpfr_bits`-bit MPFR arithmetic, step by step.

<div class="box">
**The answer in short** (`r p$seeds` seeds, `r p$rlen` passes, `r REF` &times; `r REF` maps unless said otherwise; the synthetic stand-ins of Section 2)

* **The distance is the lever, and it must sit in the update.** On the
  partial-discharge stand-in the classes were found best by the
  `r pd_best_ari$label` (ARI `r f2(pd_best_ari$value)` against `r f2(pd_eu_ari)`
  for the online SOM and `r f2(pd_dtw_ari)` for the DTW-SOM); on the gestures by
  the `r ge_best_ari$label` (`r f2(ge_best_ari$value)` against `r f2(ge_eu_ari)`).
  Against the online SOM with the same seeds, the distances that found the
  classes better on at least `r THR` of `r p$seeds` seeds were
  `r if (length(clear_pd)) paste(sapply(clear_pd, v_lab), collapse = ", ") else "none"` on the
  partial discharges, `r if (length(clear_ge)) paste(sapply(clear_ge, v_lab), collapse = ", ") else "none"`
  on the gestures and `r if (length(clear_cbf)) paste(sapply(clear_cbf, v_lab), collapse = ", ") else "none"`
  on CBF. Manhattan, Chebyshev, cosine, correlation and the shape-based
  distance each change the winner for a reason, and the update stays a
  straight line towards the item; only DTW, soft-DTW and SBD change what the
  item looks like to the prototype.
* **Detection is a different question from classification.** With a map
  trained on noise alone and the distance to the winner as the alarm, the
  `r v_lab(det_best)` map told discharges from noise best (AUROC
  `r f2(det_mean(det_best))`, online SOM `r f2(det_mean("euclid"))`).
  `r if (det_corona_eu < 0.5) sprintf("On corona alone the Euclidean alarm scores %s: a quiet corona pulse is *closer* to the noise map than noise itself, because a Euclidean distance is mostly loudness.", f2(det_corona_eu)) else sprintf("On corona alone the Euclidean alarm scores %s.", f2(det_corona_eu))`
  An amplitude-blind distance asks about the shape instead, and that is what
  detection needs.
* **Physics gives two exact temperatures and several metaphors.** Soft-DTW is
  the free energy of all alignments at a temperature gamma, and its gradient
  is the expected alignment that the update uses; deterministic annealing
  puts a temperature on the winner. Both are principled where the chaotic
  clocks were not, and both were
  tested here against the plain map that does the same job. Soft-DTW against
  the DTW-SOM, both judged with DTW, on fit: `r soft_fit`; on the classes:
  `r soft_cls`. The annealed winner against the online SOM, on order (TE):
  `r ann_te`; on fit: `r ann_qe`; on the classes: `r ann_cls`.
  `r if (temps_won == 0) "Neither temperature was clearly better than its control on any data set and any measure at this size: a principled knob is still a knob, and the test that decides is the one inside the growing DTW-SOM on the real waveforms (Section 9)." else sprintf("The temperatures were clearly better than their controls in %d of %d data-set-and-measure comparisons at this size (three maps, six measures); the rest were level or worse. The test that decides is the one inside the growing DTW-SOM on the real waveforms (Section 9).", temps_won, temps_n)`
* **The map size changes who wins.** Read the charts of Section 6 at four
  sizes before choosing: the best distance for the classes on the
  partial-discharge stand-in was `r paste(unique(sapply(size_flip[, "pd"], v_lab)), collapse = " / ")`
  from 5 &times; 5 to 14 &times; 14, and every fit measure falls with the number of
  units whatever the map does (the project's trap, Section 4 of the metrics page).
* **Precision: fp64 is the right stop.** With the same seed, the fp64
  Euclidean map chose `r flip_words(fp64_flips$flips[fp64_flips$data == "cbf" & fp64_flips$mode == "euclid"], ladder$cbf$S)`
  on the small CBF as the `r p$mpfr_bits`-bit MPFR run, and its prototypes
  ended within `r e1(max(fp64_flips$drift[fp64_flips$data == "cbf"]))` of
  it; on the PD stand-in, `r flip_words(fp64_flips$flips[fp64_flips$data == "pd" & fp64_flips$mode == "euclid"], ladder$pd$S)`.
  fp32 `r first_words(fp32_first[fp32_first$data == "cbf", ], ladder$cbf$S)`.
  The closest contest of the PD run had a relative gap of
  `r e1(gap_small["min", "pd"])` between the first and the second distance,
  `r if (gap_small["fp32", "pd"] == 0) "never inside fp32's resolution" else sprintf("inside fp32's resolution in %s of the steps", pct(gap_small["fp32", "pd"]))`
  and `r if (gap_small["fp64", "pd"] == 0) "never inside fp64's" else sprintf("inside fp64's in %s", pct(gap_small["fp64", "pd"]))`.
  The one case built to fail is raw pressure without the asinh scale, four
  decades in one squared distance: there the fp32 Euclidean map
  `r if (is.na(raw32$first_flip)) sprintf("still chose the reference's winner at every step, within %s", e1(raw32$drift)) else sprintf("chose another winner at %d of %s steps, the first at step %d", raw32$flips, format(ladder$pd_raw$S, big.mark = ","), raw32$first_flip)`,
  the fp32 DTW map `r if (is.na(raw32d$first_flip)) "did the same" else sprintf("first chose another winner at step %d", raw32d$first_flip)`,
  and fp64 `r if (raw64$flips == 0) "agreed with the reference at every step" else sprintf("differed at %d steps", raw64$flips)`. MPFR is a reference oracle
  (`r sprintf("%.1f", mpfr_secs)` s in C for what fp64 does in
  `r sprintf("%.2f", fp64_secs)` s), not a training tool; the precision
  question that matters for a field detector is the other way round, fp32 or
  fixed point on a microcontroller, with fp64 as the oracle.
* **What to build first** (Section 9), in the order the brainstorm's
  skeptics and synthesizer settled on: read the cached maps on held-out
  items with per-class confusion, detection AUROC and a sign test over the
  seeds, before any new map; then the representation ladder for partial
  discharges on the real waveforms (pulse features, envelope and
  log-spectrum, loudness as a separate coordinate, a loudness-only control);
  then shift rather than warp (SBD, or a 2 to 3% band) against the 10%
  DTW-SOM; then Heskes' energy-consistent winner at a smaller start radius;
  and for movement, dependent against independent multichannel DTW under
  the 1-NN DTW ceiling. Tier B: soft-DTW's barycentre, LVQ fine-tuning,
  U*-matrix clusters, TWED and MSM. Not first: chaos, tearing of any kind,
  MPFR training, momentum, the torus, conscience.
</div>

# 1. What the benchmarks already decided

Seven reports tested every change one at a time, seed by seed, against the
plain map that does the same job. These are the findings that bind any new
idea, with the report they come from:

# 2. The two targets and the data of this page

**Partial discharges.** The project's PD set is airborne ultrasound of
corona, air-gap and void discharges plus ambient noise, 125 samples at
500 kS/s triggered by the current pulse, loudness over four orders of
magnitude, pressure used as asinh(p / 1 mPa). A PD engineer reads three
things from such a pulse: its *shape* (rise, ringing frequency, decay, a
reflection), its *loudness*, and, when a mains-phase reference exists, its
*phase* (the PRPD pattern). The map must therefore (a) use a distance that
reads shape without being ruled by loudness, (b) keep loudness somewhere it
can be read, as a channel or a per-unit statistic, and (c) answer two
questions: *is this a discharge?* (detection, with a false-alarm rate on
noise) and *which kind?* (classification).

**Movement.** A gesture or an activity comes from several axes at once, at
its own speed, held in a sensor that is never oriented the same way twice.
The map must align in time (DTW, soft-DTW, or a rigid shift), treat the axes
together (one alignment for all channels), and be read against the 1-NN DTW
baseline that any template matcher reaches.

`r if (all(sapply(datasets, function(d) d$source == "synthetic"))) "**This knit uses synthetic stand-ins**, because the project's data (som_bench/data/datasets.rds) is not in this checkout; put it there and the loader uses the real CBF, the real partial discharges and GunPoint instead (Section 4 shows the loader)." else "**This knit uses the project's own data** where the loader found it (see the sources below)."`
Each stand-in is built to have the difficulty that matters for its target:

```{r data-table}
tab(data.frame(`Data set` = sapply(datasets, `[[`, "title"), Source = sapply(datasets, `[[`, "source"),
               Items = sapply(datasets, function(d) nrow(d$X)), Length = sapply(datasets, `[[`, "L"), Channels = sapply(datasets, `[[`, "nch"),
               Classes = sapply(datasets, function(d) nlevels(d$cls)), `DTW band` = sapply(datasets, function(d) scales_of(d)$band),
               `1-NN accuracy, Euclidean` = f3(nn_floor["euclid", ]), `1-NN accuracy, DTW` = f3(nn_floor["dtw", ]),
               `What it is` = sapply(datasets, `[[`, "about"), check.names = FALSE), search = FALSE)
```

<p class="note">1-NN accuracy: leave-one-out nearest-neighbour classification, the floor for any
map that is then read with the same distance. The gap between the Euclidean and the DTW column says
how much a time alignment can buy on each set.</p>

## A few items of every class {.tabset .tabset-pills}

```{r examples, results = "asis"}
example_plot <- function(d, per_class = 4) {
  col <- class_colours(d$cls)
  show <- unlist(lapply(split(seq_along(d$cls), d$cls), function(i) head(i, per_class)))
  pl <- plot_ly()
  for (ch in seq_len(d$nch)) for (i in show) {
    y <- d$X[i, (ch - 1) * d$L + seq_len(d$L)]
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = seq_len(d$L), y = y, type = "scatter", mode = "lines", xaxis = paste0("x", ch), yaxis = paste0("y", ch),
                    line = list(color = adjustcolor(col[[as.character(d$cls[i])]], 0.75), width = 1.3),
                    name = as.character(d$cls[i]), legendgroup = as.character(d$cls[i]), showlegend = ch == 1 && i == show[match(d$cls[i], d$cls[show])],
                    hovertemplate = paste0(as.character(d$cls[i]), ", item ", i, if (d$nch > 1) paste0(", axis ", ch), "<br>t = %{x}: %{y:.2f}<extra></extra>"))
  }
  lay <- list(margin = list(t = 20, b = 40), legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.15), showlegend = TRUE)
  for (ch in seq_len(d$nch)) {
    dom <- c((ch - 1) / d$nch + 0.02 * (ch > 1), ch / d$nch - 0.02 * (ch < d$nch))
    lay[[paste0("xaxis", if (ch > 1) ch else "")]] <- ax(if (ch == d$nch) d$x_label else NULL, domain = dom, anchor = paste0("y", ch))
    lay[[paste0("yaxis", if (ch > 1) ch else "")]] <- ax(if (d$nch > 1) paste("axis", ch) else NULL, anchor = paste0("x", ch))
  }
  slim(do.call(chart, c(list(pl), lay)))
}
for (k in names(datasets)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", SHORT[[k]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(tagList(example_plot(datasets[[k]])))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

# 3. The ideas

The brainstorm was run from seven angles, each idea then handed to a skeptic
from another angle who tried to refute it: is it already tested in the
project, is the mechanism real or a knob without a reason, are the
references right, is the control fair, does it plausibly matter for pulses
or for gestures. What survived is below; what was dropped is listed at the
end of the section with the reason. Tier A: build first; B: after A pays
off; C: a long shot worth one small experiment. Filter with the menus above
the table; the folded cells open on a click.

```{r ideas-table}
if (is.null(ideas)) {

} else {

              `L2-soft-dtw-free-energy` = "Section 6: soft-DTW SOM", `L1-free-energy-winner` = "Section 6: the annealed winner (soft arm only)",

    `In this page` = ran_of(i$id), `What it changes` = fold(paste(i$what_it_changes, i$mechanism)), `The control to beat` = fold(i$control),
```

## 3a. Distances: what each one reads, and what its update does

A SOM has two places for a distance: the **contest** (which unit wins) and
the **update** (how the item pulls the prototype). The project learned the
hard way that the two must agree. For the pointwise distances the update
needs no change: the straight line from a prototype to an item is a
geodesic of every norm, so "move a share of the way towards the item" is
the right step for L1, L2, Chebyshev and Minkowski alike; what changes is
*which* prototype moves, and that is what matters.

* **Manhattan (L1)**: the winner is the prototype with the smallest *sum of
  absolute* differences. One loud sample (a spike, a glitch) counts in
  proportion to its size, not its square, so L1 is the first thing to try
  when outliers rule the Euclidean contest. Its natural partner is the
  **clipped pull** (the Huber step of Section 4): the pull of every sample is
  capped, so one loud item cannot drag a prototype.
* **Chebyshev (L-infinity)**: only the worst sample counts. It is the
  distance of a tolerance band and is sharp on sets where one feature decides
  (a step that is or is not there), blunt where everything is noisy.
* **Minkowski p**: between the two; p = 3 is the Euclidean contest with
  large differences weighed more.
* **Cosine and correlation**: the angle between item and prototype, with or
  without their means removed. Loudness drops out entirely. For partial
  discharges that is exactly the question *is it the same shape?* asked
  without *how loud?*, which is why Section 7 finds them where it does.
  Loudness then has to be kept elsewhere: as a per-unit statistic, or as an
  extra channel (the easiest test: append asinh(peak) as a 126th value with a
  weight).
* **Shape-based distance (SBD, from k-Shape)**: one global shift instead of
  a warp, found by cross-correlation; the update shifts the item by the best
  lag. It is the rigid cousin of DTW: it reads a pulse that came 3 samples
  late as the same pulse, costs L times less than DTW, and cannot stretch
  the inside of a series. For trigger-aligned pulses with a jitter it is the
  first thing to try before DTW.
* **DTW** (the project's) and **soft-DTW**: Section 3c.
* **Not built here, worth building**: dependent *vs* independent
  multivariate DTW for the gestures (one path for all axes against one path
  per axis), MSM and TWED (elastic measures with a cost for every edit, the
  strongest in the UCR bake-offs), the lower bounds that make DTW cheap at
  mapping time (the project has LB_Keogh), and distances on transformed
  series (the log-spectrum or the envelope of a pulse, where the ringing
  frequency and the decay become positions).

## 3b. The map: growing, tearing, rejoining, and what the skeptics left of it

The project's growing DTW-SOM won on fit, order and timing; its tearing map
lost to a smaller start radius because a link broken by *length* is the
same knob as a weaker pull, applied unevenly. Tear-and-rejoin came back
from three angles in the brainstorm (GNG edge ageing by data support, a
Griffith fracture criterion on the stored strain of a link, a jigsaw step
that re-seats torn pieces before they rejoin) and every version was dropped
by its skeptic: the ageing rule's lifetime is a second schedule with no
scale of its own, the fracture rule re-parametrises the length rule, and the
jigsaw rests on a hypothesis that the tear-and-join report contradicts
(rejoined late, the disorder stays). The honest successor leaves the pull
alone and finds the walls *after* training: cluster extraction from the
U*-matrix, distance times density (Ultsch), in place of the Ward cut, tier B.
The completeness critic reinstated one version at tier B, because the user
asked for it and the project's own untested list names cutting by data
support: GNG ageing on the hexagonal lattice with the lifetime set from the
data (an edge survives as long as its two units take, on average, to win
again), the pull following graph distance over the live edges, against the
fixed lattice, on the three blobs where tearing helped and on the 18 sets
where it did not, with the number of pieces counted as in the tearing lab.
That is the one run that closes the question either way. The critic also
reinstated the window per unit for the growing map (each unit's band set
from the shifts of the items it won, births inheriting the parent's band)
and kept the torus as the rim control for Heskes' winner and for the
topographic product, which reacts to the outline of a map.

What survived for the map itself:

* **Heskes' winner** (tier A): the unit whose whole neighbourhood fits the
  item best wins, the minimum over k of &Sigma;<sub>j</sub>
  h<sub>kj</sub> d<sub>j</sub><sup>2</sup>, instead of the nearest unit. It
  makes the online SOM a gradient descent on one energy (Heskes 1999), costs
  no extra alignment (the distances are there already), and is the pairing
  that could buy fit at a smaller start radius without the order cost the
  project measured. Control: the plain map at the same start radius and at
  the default.
* **A growth-stop rule and idle-unit pruning** in the growing map (tier B):
  stop when a new unit no longer lowers the Kaski-Lagus error on held-out
  seeds; remove a unit that wins nothing for a full pass.
* **LVQ fine-tuning** when labels exist (tier B): Kohonen's LVQ1 after the
  unsupervised map, prototypes moved a little towards their own class and
  away from the others. Control: the map read by Ward clustering; purity and
  ARI on held-out items.
* **Median and relational SOMs** (tier B): prototypes that are real series,
  so that any dissimilarity serves, including TWED and MSM, which have no
  barycentre to average with.
* **Online ordering, then batch convergence** (tier B): the online schedule
  down to its radius floor, then DBA passes at frozen winners: the fit of
  batch training without its disorder.
* **Dropped, and run here anyway** (Section 6): conscience (the chaotic-units
  report already ran the bounded control, and no unit was dead to rescue)
  and the torus (the rim errors it removes are the harmless kind). Neither
  beat its control in the demonstrator. Dropped and not run: DTW neural gas
  (between the SOM and k-means by construction), bagged maps (lattice
  alignment is ill-posed on the offset hexagonal grid), a learned band per
  unit (units with different bands do not compete on one scale).

## 3c. Physics: two temperatures, one tension, and the metaphors

```{r physics-bridge, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(ideas) && nzchar(ideas$physics_bridge)) cat(ideas$physics_bridge, "\n\n")
```

The parts of that bridge that the demonstrator tests, in the words of the
code:

* <span class="chip exact">exact</span> **Soft-DTW is a free energy.** DTW
  takes the cheapest alignment; soft-DTW takes
  &minus;&gamma;&nbsp;log&nbsp;&Sigma;<sub>paths</sub>&nbsp;exp(&minus;cost/&gamma;),
  the free energy of all alignments at temperature &gamma; (Cuturi &
  Blondel 2017). Its gradient with respect to the prototype is the
  Boltzmann-weighted average of the alignments, the matrix E of the core,
  and the update of Section 4 averages the item with exactly those weights:
  the soft barycentre step. As &gamma; &rarr; 0 the path, the distance and the
  update all become DTW's (the check in Section 4 shows the two agree to
  10<sup>&minus;12</sup> at &gamma; = 0.001). One number, &gamma;, replaces the
  hard choice of one path with a smooth one; it costs about ten times DTW.
* <span class="chip exact">exact</span> **Deterministic annealing is a
  temperature on the winner.** Write the SOM's cost of assigning item x to
  unit k as E<sub>k</sub> = &Sigma;<sub>j</sub> h<sub>kj</sub> d(x, m<sub>j</sub>)<sup>2</sup>
  and let the item pull every unit with the Boltzmann weight
  P(k) &prop; exp(&minus;E<sub>k</sub>/T) (Graepel, Burger & Obermayer 1997;
  Heskes 1999 for why this is the winner that makes the SOM a gradient
  descent). At T &rarr; 0 the most probable unit takes all and the loop is
  Kohonen's; at high T every unit pulls alike and the map sits at the mean
  of the data, exactly the contracted state of the chaotic page's trap; as T
  falls the map unfolds, in order, through the phase transitions that split
  it along the principal axes of the data (Rose 1998). The radius schedule
  already plays part of this role, which is why the experiment, not the
  argument, decides whether annealing on top of a radius schedule buys
  anything: Section 6.
* <span class="chip exact">exact</span> **Heskes' winner is the zero-temperature
  limit of that assignment.** Take the unit with the lowest energy
  E<sub>k</sub> and let it win: the SOM then minimises one function, and the
  contest costs nothing beyond the distances already computed. The brainstorm
  ranks it tier A and the annealed version tier C: the hard arm first, the
  temperature only if the hard arm pays.
* <span class="chip exact">exact</span> **Magnification.** A 1-D SOM places
  prototypes with density p(x)<sup>2/3</sup> (Ritter & Schulten 1986), not
  p(x): it under-represents dense regions and over-represents sparse ones.
  Conscience pushes the exponent towards 1 (equal use of all units);
  Bauer, Der & Herrmann (1996) give a local learning rate that sets any
  exponent, including the information-optimal one for detection, where rare
  (sparse) pulses deserve more units, not fewer.
* <span class="chip metaphor">metaphor</span> **Springs and fracture.** The
  lattice as springs between prototypes with the neighbourhood as the
  stiffness, and a link that tears when its strain energy exceeds a Griffith
  threshold. Honest reading, and the skeptic's: the stiffness *is* the
  radius, and a tear by stored energy is a tear by length squared, the
  project's rule with another exponent. The elastic net of Durbin & Willshaw
  (1987) is the exact version of this energy for the ring; for a sheet it
  adds a knob, not a reason, and it was dropped.
* <span class="chip metaphor">metaphor</span> **Inertia (momentum).** A
  prototype that keeps a velocity. Cheap, so it ran in Section 6; the
  skeptic's reading is that momentum with a constant factor is a learning
  rate of &alpha;/(1 &minus; &mu;) with a lag, a reparametrisation of the
  schedule, and the results agree: no direction.
* <span class="chip metaphor">metaphor</span> **Replica exchange.** Several
  maps at different temperatures that swap; for a SOM this is *restarts with
  the best map kept*, which the ring experiments already found to be the
  working part of CHAOSOM. Dropped: the replicas would be deterministic-
  annealing runs, and the swap rule has nothing to decide that the energy
  of a single run does not. Keep the restarts, keep the best map by Heskes'
  energy, drop the exchange.

## 3d. Precision and the opposite direction

The user asked about fp64 data and an MPFR-precise map. Section 8 answers
with measurements; the reasoning is short. A SOM's state is the prototypes;
the only place a tiny numerical difference can grow is a **contest decided
by a near-tie**: if two prototypes are within the arithmetic's resolution of
each other, the winner can flip, and from that step on the two runs diverge
(the chaotic page saw the same with nudges of 10<sup>-3</sup>, and nothing
below 10<sup>-6</sup>). So the question is how often a contest is that
close, which the core now records at every step (the relative gap between
the first and the second distance). DTW adds a second place: the min over
three cells of a DP table, where a tie picks a path, but the cost is the
same whichever path is taken, and the warp differs only at ties that the
update then averages. The other direction is the one that matters for a
detector in the field: a map stored and evaluated in fp32, fp16 or
fixed-point integers on a microcontroller, with fp64 as the oracle. The
ladder of Section 8 is that oracle test run upwards. The brainstorm's one
tier-A idea here is about the data, not the arithmetic: asinh(p / 1 mPa) is
a companding law that turns four decades of loudness into about ten units,
and the question worth a table is how many bits of each class survive it
after the map's distance has done its work, which is also the question of
whether the map is a loudness meter that will not transfer out of the
anechoic chamber (Section 3a's loudness-only control answers the same
thing from the other side).

## 3e. Measuring across map sizes and for detection

* **Fair across sizes**: EV (a share, not a distance), the share of units
  used, purity against its random-units line, ARI and NMI (chance-corrected),
  and ranks within a size. Every fit measure that is a distance (QE, KL)
  falls with units; read it only within one size.
* **Trustworthiness and continuity** (Venna & Kaski 2001): are an item's k
  nearest neighbours *on the map* really its neighbours in the data
  (trustworthiness: no false neighbours), and do its k nearest neighbours
  *in the data* stay its neighbours on the map (continuity: no neighbour
  torn away)? Unlike TE they read the
  whole neighbourhood, not the runner-up alone, and unlike TP they do not
  react to the outline of the map. Computed here on the units' map
  distances against the Euclidean neighbourhoods of the items.
* **Detection**: train on the background, score every item by its distance
  to the winner, read the ROC. AUROC overall and per class: the per-class
  numbers show which discharges the map would miss.
* **Read the map on items it never saw.** Every ARI in the project's reports,
  and every one on this page, is on the training items with the number of
  classes given. The brainstorm's first experiment is to read held-out items
  (the seed's draw of items leaves a fold out), with a per-class confusion
  matrix and the detection AUROC, on the cached benchmarks: no retraining,
  and it may re-rank verdicts, because the project itself found part of
  DTW's gain in reading the map rather than training it.
* **One decision rule, stated once.** Wins seed by seed are counts, not
  p-values; under a two-sided sign test 7 of 10 seeds is p = 0.34 and 8 of
  10 is p = 0.11. So: a *win* is 9 or 10 of 10 seeds (or a paired Wilcoxon
  test at p < 0.05 whose confidence interval excludes zero); 7 or 8 of 10 is
  *undecided* and triggers a 30-seed rerun; *level* is an equivalence
  verdict, not an absence of evidence. With the `r p$seeds` seeds of this
  knit only `r p$seeds` of `r p$seeds` (p = `r signif(2 / 2^p$seeds, 2)`) is a
  statement at all, and a difference inside the seed-to-seed spread is noise
  whatever its sign. The project's summary page would lose some of its
  "helps" verdicts under this rule; that is the first thing to recount.
* **Consensus over seeds** is the cheapest ARI the cached maps can give: a
  co-association matrix over the ten Ward cuts of ten seeds, cut once, is an
  ensemble that needs no training; its controls are the single map with the
  lowest KL and a consensus of ten k-means runs, so that the gain is
  attributed to the map or to the averaging. Trustworthiness and continuity as computed here need at
  least 19 sampled items for their normalisation; the sample is 300.

```{r ideas-dropped, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(ideas) && length(ideas$dropped)) {
  cat("<details><summary>Ideas the skeptics dropped, and why</summary>\n\n")
  dr <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ideas$dropped, function(d) data.frame(Idea = d$title, Lens = d$lens, `Why it was dropped` = d$why_dropped, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
  print(tab(dr, search = TRUE))
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
if (!is.null(ideas) && length(ideas$gaps)) {
  cat("<details><summary>What the completeness critic still found missing</summary>\n\n")
  for (g in ideas$gaps) cat(sprintf("* **%s.** %s *Fix:* %s\n", g$title, g$why_it_matters, g$suggested_fix))
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```

# 4. The demonstrator

One online SOM, written once in C++ as a template over the scalar type, with
the distance as an argument of both the contest and the update, and six
ingredients (the clipped pull, conscience, the annealed winner, momentum,
the rectangular sheet, the torus) that each switch one idea on. It is not the project's core and
does not try to match it to the last bit; it follows the same conventions
(hexagonal lattice, Gaussian neighbourhood, learning rate 0.5 &rarr; 0.01,
kohonen's start radius &rarr; 0 used as 0.5 below 1, the start and the
order of items drawn from the seed), so that a variant and its control see
the same items in the same order from the same start.

```{r variants-table}
vt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(VARIANTS, function(v) data.frame(
  Variant = v$label, Group = v$group, Distance = v$mode, Lattice = paste(v$topo, if (v$torus) "torus" else "sheet"),
  Control = VARIANTS[[v$family]]$label, `What it changes` = v$what, check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
vt$Control[vt$Variant == vt$Control] <- ""
tab(vt, search = FALSE)
```

Settings that come from the data so that one value means the same thing
everywhere: the DTW band and the SBD shift are 10% of the length; soft-DTW's
&gamma; is 0.1 of the variance of one sample; the clipped pull caps each
component at one standard deviation of a sample; the annealing temperature
starts at the mean squared distance of the items to their mean (under the
map's own distance) and falls geometrically by a factor 1000 over the first
90% of the steps, then the winner is hard; conscience uses &beta; = 0.25 and
a win-share memory of 10<sup>4</sup> steps; momentum keeps half of the last
step.

**Checks.** The core's DTW equals a plain R implementation (squared local
cost, Sakoe-Chiba band) on 200 random pairs; soft-DTW converges to DTW
squared as &gamma; &rarr; 0 and its expected-alignment warp to DTW's path
average (10<sup>-12</sup> at &gamma; = 0.001); the pointwise distances equal
R's `dist()`; dependent multichannel DTW scales as it should; the online SOM
in fp64 equals the same loop written in R to the last bit; the topographic
product is 0 on an ordered chain and negative on a scrambled one; the
Kaski-Lagus way along an ordered chain is the sum of its links. The script
is `next_steps/tests/test_core.R`.

The code, in full:

```{Rcpp core-code, eval = FALSE, code = xfun::read_utf8("next_steps/ns_core.cpp")}
```

# 5. The maps, at four sizes

One figure per data set, seed 1: pick a variant in the menu and see its map
at `r paste(sprintf('%d &times; %d', SIZES, SIZES), collapse = ', ')` units side by
side. Each cell is tinted with the class of most of the items it wins (white:
none), and carries its prototype as a small curve (the first axis for the
gestures). Hover a cell for the items it won by class. Within one size,
every variant starts from the same items and sees them in the same order;
across sizes the draws differ, because a bigger map draws more start items.

## Maps {.tabset .tabset-pills}

```{r gallery, results = "asis"}
gallery_plot <- function(k) {
  d <- datasets[[k]]; col <- class_colours(d$cls); W <- 940; H <- 270; ns <- length(SIZES)
  vids <- names(VARIANTS); pl <- plot_ly(width = W, height = H); vis_group <- c()
  lay <- list(margin = list(t = 36, b = 10, l = 10, r = 10), showlegend = FALSE)
  for (si in seq_along(SIZES)) {
    s <- SIZES[si]; dom <- c((si - 1) / ns + 0.01, si / ns - 0.01)
    lay[[paste0("xaxis", if (si > 1) si else "")]] <- list(domain = dom, anchor = paste0("y", si), visible = FALSE, range = c(0.2, s + 1.3), fixedrange = TRUE)
    lay[[paste0("yaxis", if (si > 1) si else "")]] <- list(anchor = paste0("x", si), visible = FALSE, range = c(0.2, s * 0.87 + 1), fixedrange = TRUE, scaleanchor = paste0("x", si))
  }
  for (v in vids) for (si in seq_along(SIZES)) {
    s <- SIZES[si]; f <- fits[[paste(k, v, s, sep = "|")]]
    if (is.null(f)) next
    grid <- make_grid(s, s, VARIANTS[[v]]$topo, VARIANTS[[v]]$torus)
    fill <- cell_fill(f$bmu, d$cls, grid$K, col)
    counts <- table(factor(f$bmu, levels = seq_len(grid$K)), d$cls)
    hover <- sapply(seq_len(grid$K), function(u) sprintf("<b>%s, %d x %d</b><br>unit %d: %d items<br>%s", VARIANTS[[v]]$label, s, s, u, sum(counts[u, ]),
                                                          paste(sprintf("%s %d", colnames(counts), counts[u, ]), collapse = ", ")))
    pitch <- (W / ns - 20) / (s + 1.1)                                   # pixels per lattice unit in this panel
    cp <- cell_paths(grid)
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = round(cp$x, 3), y = round(cp$y, 3), type = "scatter", mode = "lines", xaxis = paste0("x", si), yaxis = paste0("y", si),
                    line = list(color = "#c3c2b7", width = 0.6), hoverinfo = "skip", visible = v == vids[1])
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = grid$pos[, 1], y = grid$pos[, 2], type = "scatter", mode = "markers", xaxis = paste0("x", si), yaxis = paste0("y", si),
                    marker = list(symbol = if (grid$topo == "hex") "hexagon" else "square", size = if (grid$topo == "hex") 0.72 * pitch else 0.9 * pitch,
                                  color = fill, line = list(width = 0)),
                    text = hover, hoverinfo = "text", visible = v == vids[1])
    cv <- proto_curves(f$M, grid, d$L, d$nch, channel = 1, y_range = range(d$X[, seq_len(d$L)]))
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = cv$x, y = cv$y, type = "scatter", mode = "lines", xaxis = paste0("x", si), yaxis = paste0("y", si),
                    line = list(color = "#D1343B", width = 1), hoverinfo = "skip", visible = v == vids[1])
    vis_group <- c(vis_group, v, v, v)
  }
  buttons <- lapply(vids, function(v) list(method = "restyle", label = VARIANTS[[v]]$label, args = list(list(visible = vis_group == v))))
  for (si in seq_along(SIZES)) lay$annotations[[si]] <- list(xref = "paper", yref = "paper", x = (si - 0.5) / ns, y = 1.0, xanchor = "center", yanchor = "bottom",
                                                           text = sprintf("%d x %d", SIZES[si], SIZES[si]), showarrow = FALSE, font = list(size = 13, color = INK2))
  lay$updatemenus <- list(menu(buttons, type = "dropdown", x = 0, y = 1.08))
  slim(do.call(chart, c(list(pl), lay)))
}
for (k in names(datasets)) {
  cat("\n\n### ", SHORT[[k]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(tagList(gallery_plot(k)))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

<p class="note">Class colours as in the examples of Section 2. The soft-DTW
map stops at 10 &times; 10 (its 14 &times; 14 map would cost about ten
minutes per seed on this machine).</p>

# 6. Every measure, every size

## 6a. One measure across the sizes

Pick the measure (the menu) and the data set (the buttons). Each line is a
variant, each point the mean over `r p$seeds` seeds at one map size, with the
range over the seeds as a band on hover. Measures that fall with the number
of units (QE, KL) are shown within one data set only; read them at one size
at a time.

```{r size-chart}
size_chart <- function() {
  vids <- names(VARIANTS); keys <- names(datasets)
  series <- list()                                            # one trace per data set and variant
  for (k in keys) for (v in vids) series[[paste(k, v)]] <- list(k = k, v = v)
  yvals <- lapply(VIEWS, function(vw) lapply(series, function(sv) {
    y <- sapply(SIZES, function(s) { x <- val(sv$k, sv$v, s, vw$m, vw$j); if (length(x)) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA })
    I(y) }))
  texts <- lapply(VIEWS, function(vw) lapply(series, function(sv) I(sapply(SIZES, function(s) {
    x <- val(sv$k, sv$v, s, vw$m, vw$j)
    if (!length(x) || all(is.na(x))) return("")
    sprintf("<b>%s</b>, %d x %d (%d units)<br>%s: %s (seeds %s to %s)", VARIANTS[[sv$v]]$label, s, s, s^2, vw$label,
            formatC(mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#"), formatC(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#"),
            formatC(max(x, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#")) }))))
  pl <- plot_ly(height = 640)
  v0 <- names(VIEWS)[1]
  for (nm in names(series)) {
    sv <- series[[nm]]; i <- match(sv$v, vids)
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = SIZES^2, y = yvals[[v0]][[nm]], text = texts[[v0]][[nm]], type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = VARIANTS[[sv$v]]$label,
                    legendgroup = sv$v, showlegend = sv$k == keys[1], visible = sv$k == keys[1], hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>",
                    line = list(color = PAL[i], width = if (VARIANTS[[sv$v]]$group == "control") 3.2 else 1.8, dash = if (VARIANTS[[sv$v]]$group == "control") "solid" else if (VARIANTS[[sv$v]]$group == "distance") "solid" else "dot"),
                    marker = list(color = PAL[i], size = 7, symbol = if (VARIANTS[[sv$v]]$mode %in% c("dtw", "softdtw")) "square" else "circle"))
  }
  measure_buttons <- lapply(names(VIEWS), function(id) list(method = "update", label = VIEWS[[id]]$label,
    args = list(list(y = unname(yvals[[id]]), text = unname(texts[[id]])),
                list(yaxis.title.text = VIEWS[[id]]$label, yaxis.type = if (VIEWS[[id]]$kind == "rel") "log" else "linear", yaxis.autorange = TRUE))))
  data_buttons <- lapply(keys, function(k) list(method = "restyle", label = SHORT[[k]], args = list(list(visible = sapply(series, function(sv) sv$k == k)))))
  chart(pl, xaxis = ax("units on the map (log scale)", type = "log", tickvals = SIZES^2, ticktext = sprintf("%d x %d", SIZES, SIZES)),
        yaxis = ax(VIEWS[[v0]]$label), legend = list(orientation = "v", x = 1.02, y = 1, yanchor = "top", font = list(size = 11), tracegroupgap = 1),
        updatemenus = list(menu(measure_buttons, type = "dropdown", x = 0, y = 1.02), menu(data_buttons, x = 0.55, y = 1.02)),
        margin = list(t = 60, r = 10, b = 50)) |> slim()
}
size_chart()
```

<p class="note">Thick lines: the two controls (online SOM, DTW-SOM). Solid
thin lines: distances; dotted: ingredients and lattices. Squares: the maps
trained with DTW or soft-DTW. Legend entries toggle a variant on all data
sets.</p>

## 6b. Every variant against its control, by data set and size

Blue: the variant beat its family's control (same seed, same start, same
order) on more seeds than it lost; red: the other way round. Pick the measure.

```{r heatmap, fig.height = 6.2}
vids <- setdiff(names(VARIANTS), c("euclid", "dtw"))
cols <- expand.grid(size = SIZES, k = names(datasets), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
col_lab <- sprintf("%s %d x %d", SHORT[cols$k], cols$size, cols$size)
cells <- lapply(names(VIEWS), function(id) {
  Z <- matrix(NA_real_, length(vids), nrow(cols)); H <- matrix("", length(vids), nrow(cols))
  for (i in seq_along(vids)) for (j in seq_len(nrow(cols))) {
    a <- tryCatch(adv_of(cols$k[j], vids[i], cols$size[j], id), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(a) || !nrow(a) || all(is.na(a$adv))) next
    Z[i, j] <- sum(a$adv > 0, na.rm = TRUE) - sum(a$adv < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
    H[i, j] <- sprintf("<b>%s</b> on %s<br>%s: better than %s on %d, worse on %d of %d seeds<br>mean %s against %s", VARIANTS[[vids[i]]]$label, col_lab[j],
                       VIEWS[[id]]$label, VARIANTS[[VARIANTS[[vids[i]]]$family]]$label, sum(a$adv > 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(a$adv < 0, na.rm = TRUE), sum(!is.na(a$adv)),
                       formatC(mean(a$v, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#"), formatC(mean(a$c, na.rm = TRUE), digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#"))
  }
  list(Z = Z, H = H)
})
names(cells) <- names(VIEWS)
ylab <- sapply(vids, function(v) VARIANTS[[v]]$label)
div_scale <- list(c(0, "#e34948"), c(0.25, "#f3aeac"), c(0.5, "#f0efec"), c(0.75, "#9ec5f4"), c(1, "#2a78d6"))
hm_buttons <- lapply(names(VIEWS), function(id) list(method = "restyle", label = VIEWS[[id]]$label, args = list(list(z = list(cells[[id]]$Z), text = list(cells[[id]]$H)))))
plot_ly(x = col_lab, y = ylab, z = cells[[1]]$Z, text = cells[[1]]$H, type = "heatmap", hoverinfo = "text", colorscale = div_scale,
        zmin = -p$seeds, zmax = p$seeds, xgap = 2, ygap = 2,
        colorbar = list(title = list(text = "seeds better minus worse than the control", side = "top", font = list(size = 12, color = INK2)),
                        orientation = "h", x = 0.5, xanchor = "center", y = -0.32, yanchor = "top", len = 0.5, thickness = 12, outlinewidth = 0,
                        tickvals = c(-p$seeds, 0, p$seeds), ticktext = c("worse on all seeds", "tie", "better on all seeds"), tickfont = list(color = INK2))) |>
  chart(xaxis = ax(NULL, tickangle = -35, showgrid = FALSE), yaxis = ax(NULL, autorange = "reversed", showgrid = FALSE, ticksuffix = "  "),
        shapes = lapply(length(SIZES) * seq_len(length(datasets) - 1), function(at) list(type = "line", xref = "x", yref = "paper", x0 = at - 0.5, x1 = at - 0.5, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = INK2, width = 1.2))),
        updatemenus = list(menu(hm_buttons, type = "dropdown", x = 0, y = 1.02)), margin = list(t = 60, r = 20, b = 150, l = 200)) |> slim()
```

<p class="note">The torus is compared with the rectangular sheet, the
rectangular sheet and all other Euclidean variants with the online SOM, the
DTW variants with the DTW-SOM. An empty cell was not run (soft-DTW at
14 &times; 14).</p>

## 6c. Seed by seed, at `r REF` &times; `r REF`

Each dot is one seed: how much better the variant did than its control with
the same start and the same order of items. Right of the line: the variant
was better. Pick the measure and the data set.

```{r strip}
strip_chart <- function(size = REF) {
  vids <- setdiff(names(VARIANTS), c("euclid", "dtw")); keys <- names(datasets); nr <- length(vids); ypos <- nr - seq_along(vids)
  vlab <- sapply(vids, v_lab)
  build <- function(k, id) {
    D <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(vids), function(r) { a <- tryCatch(adv_of(k, vids[r], size, id), error = function(e) NULL); if (is.null(a) || !nrow(a)) NULL else cbind(row = r, a) }))
    if (is.null(D)) return(NULL)
    vw <- VIEWS[[id]]; ratio <- vw$kind == "rel"
    D$x <- if (ratio) D$c / D$v else D$adv
    if (ratio && !vw$higher) D$x <- D$c / D$v else if (ratio) D$x <- D$v / D$c
    M <- aggregate(x ~ row, D, function(v) if (ratio) exp(mean(log(v))) else mean(v))
    set.seed(3)
    list(x = I(D$x), y = I(ypos[D$row] + runif(nrow(D), -0.22, 0.22)), col = I(ifelse(D$adv > 0, "#eb6834", ifelse(D$adv < 0, "#2a78d6", AXIS))),
         text = I(sprintf("<b>%s</b>, seed %d<br>variant %s, control %s", vlab[D$row], D$seed, formatC(D$v, digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#"), formatC(D$c, digits = 3, format = "fg", flag = "#"))),
         mx = I(M$x), my = I(ypos[M$row]), mtext = I(sprintf("<b>%s</b>: %s %.3g", vlab[M$row], if (ratio) "geometric mean" else "mean", M$x)),
         type = if (ratio) "log" else "linear", ref = if (ratio) 1 else 0,
         axis = if (ratio) paste(vw$label, ": control / variant (log scale; right of 1 = variant better)") else paste(vw$label, ": variant minus control (right of 0 = variant better)"))
  }
  B <- lapply(keys, function(k) { r <- lapply(names(VIEWS), build, k = k); names(r) <- names(VIEWS); r })
  names(B) <- keys
  ref_line <- function(x0) list(list(type = "line", xref = "x", yref = "paper", x0 = x0, x1 = x0, y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = INK2, width = 2)))
  pl <- plot_ly(height = 160 + 40 * nr)
  for (k in keys) {
    b <- B[[k]][[1]]
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = b$x, y = b$y, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", text = b$text, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>", visible = k == keys[1],
                    marker = list(color = b$col, size = 10, opacity = 0.85, line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 1.5)))
    pl <- add_trace(pl, x = b$mx, y = b$my, type = "scatter", mode = "markers", text = b$mtext, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>", visible = k == keys[1],
                    marker = list(color = INK, size = 14, symbol = "line-ns", line = list(color = INK, width = 3)))
  }
  measure_buttons <- lapply(names(VIEWS), function(id) {
    xs <- list(); ys <- list(); ts <- list(); cs <- list()
    for (k in keys) { b <- B[[k]][[id]]; xs <- c(xs, list(b$x, b$mx)); ys <- c(ys, list(b$y, b$my)); ts <- c(ts, list(b$text, b$mtext)); cs <- c(cs, list(b$col, INK)) }
    b1 <- B[[keys[1]]][[id]]
    list(method = "update", label = VIEWS[[id]]$label, args = list(list(x = xs, y = ys, text = ts, marker.color = cs),
                                                                   list(xaxis.title.text = b1$axis, xaxis.type = b1$type, xaxis.autorange = TRUE, shapes = ref_line(b1$ref))))
  })
  data_buttons <- lapply(keys, function(k) list(method = "restyle", label = SHORT[[k]], args = list(list(visible = rep(keys == k, each = 2)))))
  chart(pl, xaxis = ax(B[[keys[1]]][[1]]$axis), yaxis = ax(NULL, tickvals = ypos, ticktext = unname(vlab), range = c(-0.6, nr - 0.4), ticksuffix = "  ", zeroline = FALSE),
        shapes = ref_line(B[[keys[1]]][[1]]$ref), showlegend = FALSE,
        annotations = list(list(xref = "paper", yref = "paper", x = 0, y = 1.01, xanchor = "left", yanchor = "bottom", showarrow = FALSE, text = "<span style='color:#2a78d6'>&#9679;</span> control better", font = list(size = 13, color = INK)),
                           list(xref = "paper", yref = "paper", x = 1, y = 1.01, xanchor = "right", yanchor = "bottom", showarrow = FALSE, text = "variant better <span style='color:#eb6834'>&#9679;</span>", font = list(size = 13, color = INK))),
        updatemenus = list(menu(measure_buttons, type = "dropdown", x = 0, y = 1.06), menu(data_buttons, x = 0.6, y = 1.06)), margin = list(t = 80, b = 60, l = 200)) |> slim()
}
strip_chart(REF)
```

```{r all-numbers}
agg <- aggregate(cbind(QE, EV, TE, KL, TP, used, purity, ARI, NMI, trust, cont, seconds, comparisons, not_nearest, gap_median, gap_tiny) ~ dataset + variant + size + judge,
                 data = bench, FUN = function(v) mean(v, na.rm = TRUE), na.action = na.pass)

agg$Map <- factor(sprintf("%d x %d", agg$size, agg$size), levels = sprintf("%d x %d", SIZES, SIZES)); agg$Judge <- factor(JUDGE_LAB[agg$judge], levels = JUDGE_LAB)
out <- agg[order(agg$`Data set`, agg$Map, agg$Variant, agg$Judge), c("Data set", "Map", "Variant", "Judge", "QE", "EV", "TE", "KL", "TP", "used", "purity", "ARI", "NMI", "trust", "cont", "seconds", "not_nearest", "gap_tiny")]

names(out)[names(out) == "seconds"] <- "Seconds"; names(out)[names(out) == "not_nearest"] <- "Winner not nearest"; names(out)[names(out) == "gap_tiny"] <- "Contests closer than 1e-6"
```
