```{r results-text, include = FALSE}
# the sentences of the box below, from the results
best_by <- function(k, view, size = REF) { b <- best_variant(k, size, view); sprintf("%s (%s)", b$label, formatC(b$value, digits = 2, format = "f")) }
ctrl_of <- function(k, view, size = REF) formatC(mean_of(k, "euclid", size, view), digits = 2, format = "f")
soft_vs_dtw <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "softdtw", REF, "qe_dtw"))
anneal_te <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "anneal", REF, "te_own")); anneal_qe <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "anneal", REF, "qe_eu"))
cos_pd <- wins_of("pd", "cosine", REF, "ari_own"); sbd_pd <- wins_of("pd", "sbd", REF, "ari_own"); l1_pd <- wins_of("pd", "manhattan", REF, "ari_own")
dtw_pd_wins <- wins_vs("pd", "dtw", "euclid", REF, "ari_own")
sbd_ge <- wins_of("gestures", "sbd", REF, "ari_own"); dtw_ge <- wins_vs("gestures", "dtw", "euclid", REF, "ari_own"); cor_ge <- wins_of("gestures", "correlation", REF, "ari_own")
hub_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "huber", REF, "ari_own")); l1h_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "l1_huber", REF, "ari_own"))
ann_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "anneal", REF, "ari_own")); dan_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "dtw_anneal", REF, "ari_own"))
tor_qe <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "torus", REF, "qe_eu")); tor_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "torus", REF, "ari_own"))
rect_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "rect", REF, "ari_own")); con_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "conscience", REF, "ari_own"))
mom_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "momentum", REF, "ari_own"))
l1_qe <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "manhattan", REF, "qe_eu")); l1_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "manhattan", REF, "ari_own"))
hub_qe <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "huber", REF, "qe_eu")); con_used <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "conscience", REF, "used_own"))
tor_te <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "torus", REF, "te_own")); rect_te <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "rect", REF, "te_own"))
mom_qe <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "momentum", REF, "qe_eu")); mom_te <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "momentum", REF, "te_own"))
soft_te <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "softdtw", REF, "te_dtw")); soft_ari <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "softdtw", REF, "ari_dtw"))
dan_te <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "dtw_anneal", REF, "te_own")); dan_qe <- sapply(names(datasets), function(k) wins_of(k, "dtw_anneal", REF, "qe_dtw"))
fmt_w <- function(w) if (is.null(dim(w))) sprintf("%d of %d", w[["better"]], w[["n"]]) else paste(sprintf("%d of %d", w["better", ], w["n", ]), collapse = ", ")
secs_ratio <- function(v, k = "pd", size = REF) mean_of(k, v, size, "secs") / mean_of(k, "euclid", size, "secs")
```

<div class="box">

Counts are seeds on which the variant beat its control, out of `r p$seeds`,
at `r REF` &times; `r REF`, in the order `r paste(SHORT, collapse = ", ")`.

* **Distances.** The classes of the partial-discharge stand-in were found
  best by `r best_by("pd", "ari_own")`, of the gestures by
  `r best_by("gestures", "ari_own")`, of CBF by `r best_by("cbf", "ari_own")`
  (ARI with each map's own distance; online SOM `r ctrl_of("pd", "ari_own")`,
  `r ctrl_of("gestures", "ari_own")` and `r ctrl_of("cbf", "ari_own")`).
  Against the online SOM on the PD classes: cosine `r fmt_w(cos_pd)`, SBD
  `r fmt_w(sbd_pd)`, Manhattan `r fmt_w(l1_pd)`, the DTW-SOM `r fmt_w(dtw_pd_wins)`;
  on the gestures: SBD `r fmt_w(sbd_ge)`, the DTW-SOM `r fmt_w(dtw_ge)`,
  correlation `r fmt_w(cor_ge)`. SBD costs
  `r sprintf("%.0f", secs_ratio("sbd"))` times the online SOM, DTW
  `r sprintf("%.0f", secs_ratio("dtw"))` times, soft-DTW
  `r sprintf("%.0f", secs_ratio("softdtw"))` times.
* **Manhattan and the clipped pull.** Manhattan against the online SOM:
  classes `r fmt_w(l1_ari)`; fit judged with the Euclidean distance
  `r fmt_w(l1_qe)` (its rival's own distance, where it cannot win by
  construction). The clipped pull alone: fit `r fmt_w(hub_qe)`, classes
  `r fmt_w(hub_ari)`; Manhattan with the clipped pull: classes
  `r fmt_w(l1h_ari)`. On data with few outliers an L1 contest is a different
  contest, not a better one; the clipped pull is the cheaper of the two to
  keep.
* **The two temperatures.** Soft-DTW against the DTW-SOM, both read with
  DTW: fit `r fmt_w(soft_vs_dtw)`, order (TE) `r fmt_w(soft_te)`, classes
  (ARI) `r fmt_w(soft_ari)`. The annealed winner on the Euclidean map: order
  `r fmt_w(anneal_te)`, fit `r fmt_w(anneal_qe)`, classes `r fmt_w(ann_ari)`;
  on the DTW-SOM: order `r fmt_w(dan_te)`, fit `r fmt_w(dan_qe)`, classes
  `r fmt_w(dan_ari)`. The annealed contest chose a unit other than the nearest
  in `r pct(mean(bench$not_nearest[bench$variant == "anneal" & bench$judge == "own"]))`
  of the steps: it is a different map, and on these data at this size not a
  better one. Both are worth one more test where a wrong early winner costs
  most, inside the growing map.
* **Lattices.** The torus against the rectangular sheet: order (TE)
  `r fmt_w(tor_te)`, fit `r fmt_w(tor_qe)`, classes `r fmt_w(tor_ari)`; the
  rectangular sheet against the hexagonal one: order `r fmt_w(rect_te)`,
  classes `r fmt_w(rect_ari)`. With four neighbours instead of six, TE counts
  more runner-ups as errors, so compare the two sheets on KL and on trust,
  not on TE alone.
* **Conscience** used more of the map on `r fmt_w(con_used)` seeds and found
  the classes better on `r fmt_w(con_ari)`; **momentum**: fit (Euclidean QE)
  `r fmt_w(mom_qe)`, order `r fmt_w(mom_te)`, classes `r fmt_w(mom_ari)`.

</div>

# 7. Detection: a map trained on noise

For partial discharges the first question is not *which kind* but *is it
one*. The simplest detector a SOM offers: train on the background (the noise
class only), then score every waveform by its distance to its winner; a
discharge should land far from every prototype of noise. Each variant,
7 &times; 7 maps, `r p$seeds` seeds, the AUROC of that score for discharges
against noise, overall and per kind:

```{r detection, fig.height = 5}
BASE_LAB <- c(base_peak = "Control: loudness (peak of the series)", base_1nn_euclid = "Control: nearest noise item, Euclidean",
              base_1nn_cosine = "Control: nearest noise item, cosine", base_1nn_dtw = "Control: nearest noise item, DTW")
det_lab <- function(v) if (v %in% names(VARIANTS)) VARIANTS[[v]]$label else BASE_LAB[[v]]
dv <- names(VARIANTS); da <- aggregate(. ~ variant, data = det[, c("variant", grep("^AUROC", names(det), value = TRUE))], FUN = mean)
da <- da[order(-da$AUROC), ]
pl <- plot_ly(height = 480)
for (v in da$variant) {
  d <- det[det$variant == v, ]; is_base <- !(v %in% dv)
  pl <- add_trace(pl, x = d$AUROC, y = rep(det_lab(v), nrow(d)), type = "scatter", mode = "markers", name = det_lab(v), showlegend = FALSE,
                  marker = list(color = if (is_base) MUTED else PAL[match(v, dv)], size = if (is_base) 12 else 10, symbol = if (is_base) "diamond" else "circle",
                                opacity = 0.85, line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 1.5)),
                  text = sapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) sprintf("<b>%s</b>%s<br>AUROC %.3f<br>%s", det_lab(v), if (is_base) "" else sprintf(", seed %d", d$seed[i]), d$AUROC[i],
                                 paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", sub("AUROC_", "", grep("^AUROC_", names(d), value = TRUE)), as.numeric(d[i, grep("^AUROC_", names(d))])), collapse = ", "))),
                  hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>")
}
chart(pl, xaxis = ax("AUROC of the score as a discharge alarm (1 = perfect, 0.5 = chance)", range = c(0, 1.02)),
      yaxis = ax(NULL, categoryorder = "array", categoryarray = rev(sapply(da$variant, det_lab)), ticksuffix = "  "),
      shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = 0.5, x1 = 0.5, yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = AXIS, dash = "dot"))), margin = list(t = 20, l = 250)) |> slim()
dat <- da; dat$variant <- sapply(dat$variant, det_lab); names(dat) <- c("Score", "AUROC, all discharges", paste("AUROC,", sub("AUROC_", "", names(dat)[-(1:2)])))
tab(dat, search = FALSE, digits = setNames(as.list(rep(3, ncol(dat) - 1)), names(dat)[-1]))
det_som <- det[det$variant %in% dv, ]
det_mean <- function(v) mean(det$AUROC[det$variant == v])
det_best <- names(which.max(sapply(dv, det_mean)))
base_best <- names(which.max(sapply(names(BASE_LAB), det_mean)))
```

Grey diamonds are the controls that are not maps: the loudness of the
series as the alarm (the first detector a PD engineer would try), and the
distance to the nearest noise item under the Euclidean, cosine and DTW
distances (a noise item is scored against the other noise items). A map
earns its place only above those.

<div class="box">

* The `r v_lab(det_best)` map is the best alarm among the maps (AUROC
  `r f3(det_mean(det_best))`); the online SOM reaches `r f3(det_mean("euclid"))`.
  The best control that is not a map is `r tolower(sub("Control: ", "", BASE_LAB[[base_best]]))`
  (`r f3(det_mean(base_best))`); the loudness threshold alone scores
  `r f3(det_mean("base_peak"))`. So
  `r if (det_mean(det_best) > det_mean(base_best) + 0.01) "the map adds something over the nearest-neighbour score under the same distance" else if (det_mean(det_best) >= det_mean(base_best) - 0.01) "the map and the nearest-neighbour score under the same distance are level, so the distance is the finding, not the map" else "the nearest-neighbour score beats the map, so the distance is the finding and the map costs accuracy for its summary"`. Per kind, the Euclidean
  alarm scores `r f3(det_corona_eu)` on corona`r if (det_corona_eu < 0.5) ": below 0.5 means a corona pulse lies *closer* to the noise prototypes than noise does, because it is quiet and a Euclidean distance is mostly loudness" else ""`.
  An amplitude-blind distance (cosine, correlation, SBD) asks about the shape
  instead`r if (det_corona_eu < 0.5) ", and the quiet pulses come back" else ""`.
* This is the one place on this page where the distances differ by a wide
  margin, and the one that matters first in the field. The roadmap's first
  experiment is this test on the real waveforms, with a false-alarm rate at
  a fixed detection rate next to the AUROC.

</div>

# 8. The precision ladder

```{r ladder-table}
lt <- lad_tab
lt$data <- c(cbf = sprintf("%s, %d x %d, %d passes", small_cbf$title, LADDER$cbf$size, LADDER$cbf$size, LADDER$cbf$rlen),
             pd = sprintf("partial-discharge stand-in (600 x 125, asinh scale), %d x %d, %d passes", LADDER$pd$size, LADDER$pd$size, LADDER$pd$rlen),
             pd_raw = sprintf("the same pulses as raw pressure in mPa (no asinh), %d x %d, %d passes", LADDER$pd_raw$size, LADDER$pd_raw$size, LADDER$pd_raw$rlen))[lt$data]
lt$drift <- formatC(lt$drift, digits = 2, format = "e"); lt$flip_share <- NULL
names(lt) <- c("Data", "Distance", "Arithmetic", "Reference", "First step with another winner", "Steps with another winner", "Largest difference of a prototype", "QE", "TE", "Seconds")
tab(lt, search = FALSE, digits = list(QE = 4, TE = 4, Seconds = 2))
```

The same seed, the same start, the same order of items, trained at every
precision; "another winner" is counted against the `r p$mpfr_bits`-bit MPFR
run, which repeats the core's operations one by one in the MPFR library
(`next_steps/ns_mpfr.cpp`); the row "Rmpfr check" is the same loop written
in R with the Rmpfr package, an independent check of that code. The largest
difference of a prototype is over all units and all values at the end.

```{r ladder-curves, fig.height = 4.6}
cv <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(LD), function(k) cbind(data = k, ladder[[k]]$curves)))
cv$drift[cv$drift <= 0] <- NA
precs <- unique(cv$precision)
pl <- plot_ly(height = 400)
for (dk in names(LD)) for (mo in c("euclid", "dtw")) for (pr in precs) {
  d <- cv[cv$data == dk & cv$mode == mo & cv$precision == pr, ]
  if (!nrow(d) || all(is.na(d$drift))) next
  pl <- add_trace(pl, x = d$step, y = d$drift, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = pr, legendgroup = pr, showlegend = dk == "cbf" && mo == "euclid",
                  visible = dk == "cbf" && mo == "euclid", line = list(color = PAL[match(pr, precs)], width = 2), marker = list(color = PAL[match(pr, precs)], size = 6),
                  text = sprintf("%s, %s<br>step %d: largest difference %.2e", pr, mo, d$step, d$drift), hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>")
}
groups <- unlist(lapply(names(LD), function(dk) lapply(c("euclid", "dtw"), function(mo) sapply(precs, function(pr) { d <- cv[cv$data == dk & cv$mode == mo & cv$precision == pr, ]; nrow(d) > 0 && !all(is.na(d$drift)) }))), recursive = FALSE)
keys4 <- as.vector(outer(c("euclid", "dtw"), names(LD), function(m, d) paste(d, m)))[c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6)]
labs4 <- as.vector(t(outer(unname(LD), c("Euclidean", "DTW"), paste, sep = ", ")))
vis_all <- unlist(lapply(seq_along(groups), function(i) rep(i, sum(groups[[i]]))))
buttons <- lapply(seq_along(keys4), function(i) list(method = "restyle", label = labs4[i], args = list(list(visible = vis_all == i))))
chart(pl, xaxis = ax("training step (log scale)", type = "log"), yaxis = ax("largest difference from the reference (log)", type = "log", exponentformat = "power"),
      updatemenus = list(menu(buttons, x = 0, y = 1.03)), legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.25), margin = list(t = 50, b = 70)) |> slim()
```

```{r gap-hist, fig.height = 3.8}
gh <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(LD), function(k) rbind(data.frame(data = LD[[k]], mode = "Euclidean", gap = ladder[[k]]$gap), data.frame(data = LD[[k]], mode = "DTW", gap = ladder[[k]]$gap_dtw))))
gh <- gh[is.finite(gh$gap) & gh$gap > 0, ]
pl <- plot_ly(height = 330)
i <- 0
for (dk in unique(gh$data)) for (mo in unique(gh$mode)) {
  i <- i + 1; g <- gh$gap[gh$data == dk & gh$mode == mo]
  pl <- add_trace(pl, x = log10(g), type = "histogram", name = paste(dk, mo), opacity = 0.55, nbinsx = 60, marker = list(color = PAL[i]),
                  hovertemplate = paste(dk, mo, "<br>log10 gap %{x}: %{y} steps<extra></extra>"))
}
chart(pl, barmode = "overlay", xaxis = ax("log10 of the relative gap between the first and the second distance in a contest"), yaxis = ax("steps"),
      shapes = list(list(type = "line", x0 = log10(2^-23), x1 = log10(2^-23), yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = INK2, dash = "dot")),
                    list(type = "line", x0 = log10(2^-52), x1 = log10(2^-52), yref = "paper", y0 = 0, y1 = 1, line = list(color = INK2, dash = "dot"))),
      annotations = list(list(x = log10(2^-23), y = 1, yref = "paper", text = "fp32 resolution", showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "left", font = list(size = 11, color = INK2)),
                         list(x = log10(2^-52), y = 1, yref = "paper", text = "fp64 resolution", showarrow = FALSE, xanchor = "left", font = list(size = 11, color = INK2))),
      legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.3), margin = list(t = 20, b = 70)) |> slim()
```

```{r ladder-text, include = FALSE}
row_of <- function(dk, mo, pr) lad_tab[lad_tab$data == dk & lad_tab$mode == mo & lad_tab$precision == pr, ]
fp32c <- row_of("cbf", "euclid", "fp32"); fp32p <- row_of("pd", "euclid", "fp32"); fp32d <- row_of("pd", "dtw", "fp32")
fp64c <- row_of("cbf", "euclid", "fp64"); fp64p <- row_of("pd", "euclid", "fp64"); fp64d <- row_of("pd", "dtw", "fp64"); fp64cd <- row_of("cbf", "dtw", "fp64")
kah <- row_of("pd", "euclid", "fp64 + Kahan"); d32 <- row_of("pd", "euclid", "fp32 data, fp64 arithmetic"); d32c <- row_of("cbf", "euclid", "fp32 data, fp64 arithmetic")
q_te <- function(dk, mo) range(lad_tab$TE[lad_tab$data == dk & lad_tab$mode == mo]); q_qe <- function(dk, mo) range(lad_tab$QE[lad_tab$data == dk & lad_tab$mode == mo])
gap_pd <- gap_small[, "pd"]
```

<div class="box">

* **fp64, 80-bit, 128-bit and MPFR agree.** On the small CBF the fp64
  Euclidean map chose `r flip_words(fp64c$flips, ladder$cbf$S)` as the
  `r p$mpfr_bits`-bit run, and its prototypes end within `r e1(fp64c$drift)` of
  the reference; on the PD stand-in `r flip_words(fp64p$flips, ladder$pd$S)`
  (drift `r e1(fp64p$drift)`); under DTW, `r fp64cd$flips` and `r fp64d$flips`
  steps differ. The Rmpfr loop agreed with the MPFR core
  `r if (nrow(rmpfr_row) && rmpfr_row$flips[1] == 0 && rmpfr_row$drift[1] == 0) "on every winner and every bit of every prototype" else sprintf("except for %d winners and a drift of %s", rmpfr_row$flips[1], e1(rmpfr_row$drift[1]))`
  (`r sprintf("%.0f", rmpfr_row$seconds[1])` s against `r sprintf("%.1f", mpfr_secs)` s in C). Kahan summation changed
  `r if (kah$flips == fp64p$flips && abs(kah$drift - fp64p$drift) < 1e-14) "nothing" else sprintf("the count to %d and the drift to %s", kah$flips, e1(kah$drift))`.
  The measures of all these runs agree to the digits shown (TE from
  `r f3(q_te("pd", "euclid")[1])` to `r f3(q_te("pd", "euclid")[2])` on the PD stand-in across
  every arithmetic including fp32).
* **fp32 drifts, and it does not matter.** The fp32 Euclidean run
  `r first_words(fp32c, ladder$cbf$S)` on the small CBF, and
  `r first_words(fp32p, ladder$pd$S)` on the PD stand-in
  (under DTW: `r if (is.na(fp32d$first_flip)) "no other winner either" else sprintf("another winner first at step %d", fp32d$first_flip)`).
  The curves show the drift growing from 10<sup>-6</sup> as the training goes
  on. Where a winner does flip, the map that follows is a different map, not
  a worse one: the spread between seeds is far larger than the spread between
  arithmetics.
* **Raw pressure is the case built to fail, and it is the one to watch.**
  Without the asinh scale the loudest sample of an air-gap pulse squared is
  10<sup>8</sup> times a corona sample squared, so one squared distance mixes
  numbers that fp32 cannot add. On the same pulses as raw pressure fp32
  `r if (is.na(raw32$first_flip)) sprintf("still chose the reference's winner at every step (drift %s)", e1(raw32$drift)) else sprintf("chose another winner at %d of %s steps, the first at step %d, and drifted to %s", raw32$flips, format(ladder$pd_raw$S, big.mark = ","), raw32$first_flip, e1(raw32$drift))`;
  under DTW `r if (is.na(raw32d$first_flip)) "no other winner" else sprintf("another winner first at step %d", raw32d$first_flip)`;
  fp64 `r if (raw64$flips == 0) "still agreed with the reference at every step" else sprintf("differed at %d steps", raw64$flips)`.
  The lesson is the project's asinh scale, not a precision upgrade: compand
  the data and fp32 is enough; feed a map raw pressure over four decades and
  fp32 is not, but neither is the map, because it is then a loudness meter.
* **fp64 data make no difference either.** Rounding every value of the data
  (items and start alike) to fp32 and training in fp64 gave `r d32$flips`
  other winners on the PD stand-in and `r d32c$flips` on CBF: the data of a
  16-bit or 24-bit converter carry nothing that fp64 arithmetic cannot keep.
* **Why.** `r if (gap_pd["fp32"] == 0) sprintf("No contest of the PD run came closer than fp32's resolution (2<sup>-23</sup>); the closest had a relative gap of %s", e1(gap_pd["min"])) else sprintf("A contest closer than fp32's resolution (2<sup>-23</sup>) happened in %s of the steps of the PD run", pct(gap_pd["fp32"]))`,
  and `r if (gap_pd["fp64"] == 0) "none came near fp64's (2<sup>-52</sup>)" else sprintf("%s came closer than fp64's (2<sup>-52</sup>)", pct(gap_pd["fp64"]))`;
  the histogram puts nearly every contest between 10<sup>-3</sup> and 1.
  Winners flip at near-ties, near-ties are rare, and when one flips the map
  that follows is one more seed, not a broken one.
* **So:** fp64 is the right precision to train in; MPFR is the oracle to
  prove it (`r sprintf("%.0f", mpfr_secs)` s for `r format(ladder$cbf$S, big.mark = ",")`
  steps of a 7 &times; 7 map, against milliseconds), useful once per core
  change, not for training. The experiment to run next is downwards: the
  trained map stored as fp16 or as 16-bit fixed point and evaluated on a
  microcontroller, with the fp64 winners as the truth and the count of
  flips as the score, because that is where a PD detector will live.

</div>

# 9. The roadmap

```{r tiers, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(ideas) && length(ideas$tiers)) {
  title_of <- function(id) { i <- Filter(function(x) x$id == id, ideas$ideas); if (length(i)) i[[1]]$title else id }
  for (t in ideas$tiers) {
    cat(sprintf("**Tier %s.** %s\n\n", t$tier, gsub("\n+", "\n\n", t$rationale)))
    cat(sprintf("<p class='note'>Ideas of this tier (%d): %s.</p>\n\n", length(t$ids), paste(sapply(t$ids, title_of), collapse = " &middot; ")))
  }
  cat("<details><summary>The five to start with for partial discharges, and the five for movement</summary>\n\n")
  pick <- function(ids) paste(sapply(ids, function(id) { i <- Filter(function(x) x$id == id, ideas$ideas); if (length(i)) i[[1]]$title else id }), collapse = "; ")
  cat("* **Partial discharges:** ", pick(ideas$pd_top5), "\n* **Movement:** ", pick(ideas$movement_top5), "\n\n</details>\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

<div class="box">

**How to run each experiment**, in the project's way: the same seeds, the
variant against the control that does the same job without the new
ingredient, the start and the order of items drawn from the seed, every map
judged with the Euclidean distance, with DTW and with its own, QE next to TE
(or KL), ARI when the classes are known and now on held-out items, AUROC and
the per-class misses when the question is detection; counts of seeds better
and worse with a sign test, never a mean alone; and the same experiment at
two map sizes, because Section 6 shows the ranking move with the size.

1. **Reading and statistics first** (tier A, a day, no training): the
   cached benchmarks of the project and of this page read on held-out items,
   with per-class confusion, the novelty AUROC against the non-map controls
   of Section 7, consensus over the seeds, and the decision rule of Section
   3e. The real PD set has 850 untouched waveforms per class beyond the 150
   the benchmark drew: train on the 150, test on the 850, and report the
   false-alarm rate at 1% with real counts. Expect some of the summary's
   "helps" verdicts to become "undecided", and a 30-seed rerun of the few
   that matter.
2. **The representation ladder for partial discharges** (tier A, two days):
   on the real waveforms, a map on pulse-shape features (rise, decay,
   dominant frequency, energy, the time-frequency map of Contin and
   colleagues), one on the envelope and the log-spectrum, one on the series
   with loudness as a separate weighted coordinate, and the loudness-only
   control (log peak, Ward cut), against the Euclidean and the DTW-SOM. If a
   five-number map matches the DTW-SOM's ARI, the elastic family is moot on
   this data. The demonstrator's evidence for this order: the amplitude-blind
   distances led detection by a wide margin (Section 7). One question to the
   data's owners first: do the recordings carry the mains phase, the apparent
   charge or a timestamp per pulse? If they do, the phase-resolved pattern is
   the field's standard feature and belongs in the ladder as a circular
   coordinate, which is where the torus earns its place.
3. **Shift, not warp** (tier A, a day): SBD and a 2 to 3% DTW band against
   the 10% DTW-SOM on the real pulses, with a per-class histogram of the
   best shift. Trigger-aligned pulses jitter by a few samples; that is a
   shift, not a warp. In the demonstrator SBD was level with or ahead of the
   DTW-SOM on the PD classes at a fraction of the cost (Section 6).
4. **Heskes' winner** (tier A, two days): the energy-consistent winner at
   half and a quarter of the start radius, against the plain map at the same
   radius and at the default, on QE and TE together. The only change to the
   map's own rule that the skeptics kept at tier A.
5. **The input layer for movement** (tier A, two days): dependent against
   independent multichannel DTW on real gesture sets, with the check that
   dependent DTW at band 0 equals the stacked Euclidean map to the last bit,
   the 1-NN DTW ceiling, per-class held-out confusion with leave-subjects-out
   folds, and the engineer's control that PD has and movement lacked: a
   Euclidean map on windowed features (per-axis mean, spread, energy,
   dominant frequency, inter-axis correlations, the magnitude channel), with
   a supervised ceiling on the same features.
6. **Tier B, after the tables above**: soft-DTW's expected-alignment update
   inside the growing map (hard winner kept), priced warps (TWED, MSM),
   slope-constrained steps and open ends for gestures (with the project's
   derivative-DTW variant as the control row, since it attacked the same
   pinch and won once, on the solar I-V curves), LVQ fine-tuning, U*-matrix
   cluster extraction, a growth-stop rule and idle-unit pruning, the window
   per unit, GNG edges with a data-set lifetime (the one tear-and-rejoin
   left standing), median and relational maps.
   **One rule for all of them:** any ingredient that wins on the fixed map is
   re-run inside the growing DTW-SOM, the project's best map, with its births
   using the ingredient's own distance or barycentre, against the plain
   growing map with the same seeds.
7. **Tier C, one small run each**: 1-D Wasserstein on energy profiles,
   coarse-to-fine training on the envelope, a streaming growing map, the
   fixed-point Manhattan map for a field detector, the annealed winner, and
   the precision ladder as a falsification test on the real data.
8. **Not worth the time** on the evidence here and in the project: MPFR
   training, momentum, tearing by any rule tried so far, chaos of any kind,
   the torus, conscience, a PCA start.

</div>

# 10. Limits

* **Synthetic stand-ins.** The partial discharges and the gestures of this
  knit are generated to have the difficulty that matters (loudness over four
  decades with shape as the signal; speed, amplitude and orientation changes
  with shape as the signal), not to be the real data. Every number above is
  a statement about the demonstrator on these sets; the roadmap's first step
  repeats the study on the real waveforms. The loader swaps them in when
  `som_bench/data/datasets.rds` is present.
* **One setting of everything**: 10% band, `r p$rlen` passes, one schedule,
  &gamma; = 0.1 of a sample's variance, one temperature schedule, one clip,
  one conscience, `r p$seeds` seeds. Each of these would move some results;
  the project's window study shows how much one of them can.
* **The demonstrator is a fixed-size online map.** The growing DTW-SOM, the
  project's best, is where the winners of this page should go; it is not
  rebuilt here, and nothing above says how an ingredient behaves while a map
  grows.
* **The idea catalogue is a brainstorm**, verified by skeptics for mechanism,
  prior testing and fair controls, with references marked where they could
  not be checked. It ranks by expected value per hour of your time, which is
  a judgement, not a measurement.
* **A contest's gap** (Section 8 and the last column of the big table) is
  the second distance minus the first, over the magnitude of the first; for
  soft-DTW, whose values can be negative, it is a ratio of the same kind but
  not on the same scale as a distance.
* **The measure list and the size grid are this page's, not the project's.**
  The timing error (CBF), the spread (colours), the pieces (torn maps) and
  the tour gap (rings) are not computed here, and the sizes are 5, 7, 10 and
  14 a side where the benchmark used one rule of about 5&radic;N units. The
  roadmap's tables should carry every set-specific measure whenever its set
  is run, and keep CBF and the colours as sanity sets, because they catch
  smearing and shape loss that the PD and gesture sets do not.
* **Times** are from `r cores` parallel processes on this machine
  (`r format(n_maps, big.mark = ",")` maps in `r sprintf("%.0f", cpu_min)` CPU
  minutes); the number of comparisons is the fair cost.
